task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 31, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper explainer answering why Ashcombe businesses will not all see their water bills move in the same direction under the new commercial tariff.

facts.text: Ashcombe Water Board's commercial tariff takes effect Oct. 1, 2026, following its August budget decision.
The monthly fixed commercial charge rises from $35 to $50, while the usage charge falls from $3 to $2.50 per 1,000 gallons.
For an account using 20,000 gallons, those charges produce a water-only bill of $100 instead of $95.
For an account using 200,000 gallons, they produce a water-only bill of $550 instead of $635.
The examples hold water use constant and exclude sewer charges, which are billed separately under an unchanged schedule.
At 30,000 gallons a month, the old and new water-only charges are both $125.
Below that usage point the new formula costs more; above it the new formula costs less, before separate charges.
Residential accounts retain their current tariff and are not included in this commercial change.
The board says a larger fixed charge is intended to collect more revenue for pipes and treatment capacity that must be maintained regardless of monthly use.
The board's budget does not project the same percentage change for every commercial customer's bill.
Mallow Street Bakery averages about 20,000 gallons a month and cannot reduce its fixed charge by using less water.
Bakery owner Deni Rook said she still sees value in repairing leaks because the usage portion of the bill remains.
Rook said, "The first fifty dollars arrives before we turn on a tap."
Linen processor Vale Washworks uses about 200,000 gallons in a typical month but has substantial seasonal variation.
Its manager cautioned that a lower tariff at constant use does not guarantee a lower actual bill in a busier month.
Board finance officer Tera Linn said, "We changed the balance between keeping the system ready and charging for each gallon."
Businesses with separate meters receive a fixed charge on each account under both the old and new schedules.
The board offers account-specific estimates using the previous year's monthly readings, not a guarantee of future consumption.
Ashcombe's oldest pumping station remains in service as a backup during maintenance.
No new mandatory meter installation fee or change in water quality is part of this tariff decision.
